title: Products with Zero Total Sales
description:
Find products that have **no sales at all** — they never appeared in `order_items`. Return their name and category.

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`, `category`, `price`, `stock_quantity`

**Table: order_items** — `id`, `order_id`, `product_id`, `quantity`, `unit_price`

Output columns: `name`, `category`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, stock_quantity INT); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Laptop','Electronics',999.99,10),(2,'Phone','Electronics',699.99,25),(3,'Desk','Furniture',299.99,5),(4,'Chair','Furniture',149.99,8),(5,'Monitor','Electronics',349.99,15); CREATE TABLE order_items (id INT, order_id INT, product_id INT, quantity INT, unit_price DECIMAL); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,1,1,1,999.99),(2,1,2,2,699.99),(3,2,3,1,299.99);
solution_sql: SELECT p.name, p.category FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.id IS NULL ORDER BY p.name

test_cases.description: Chair and Monitor have no sales

hints: LEFT JOIN from products to order_items keeps all products.
WHERE oi.id IS NULL filters to products with no matching order_items row.
explanation: A LEFT JOIN retains all products. Products 4 (Chair) and 5 (Monitor) have no order_items matches, so oi.id is NULL for them. The WHERE clause isolates these unsold products.
